messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa** (about 0.1 atm), the freezing point of water is slightly below 0 °C.  
Using the slope of the ice‑water melting curve near atmospheric pressure (≈ –0.0075 °C kPa⁻¹), the freezing point drops by roughly 0.7 °C compared to the standard 0 °C at 1 atm.  

**Freezing point ≈ –0.7 °C** (approximately –0.68 °C).
